# Motion QA

The motion primitives (`./README.md`) are the ground truth every component
moves by, so they are held in six layers, each one a test that runs in CI's
`tests` job: `npm --prefix app test` (Vitest) and `npm --prefix app run
test:e2e` (the build, then Playwright). Nothing reaches the network; the
browser layers run on the kit's catalog, built on its own
(`vite.kit.config.ts`, previewed on a second free port by
`playwright.config.ts`, never shipped), and on real screens with the e2e
fakes.

Below the layers is every defect they caught when they went in (the owner
had seen most of them in a recording of the catalog and the window:
flicker, restarts, two copies, a misbehaving tab pill, a rubber band out of
place, things out of their box, old and new overlapping). Each row is the
defect, why it happened, the test that now fails if it comes back, and the
fix, which is always in the primitive rather than in a screen. Every one of
these tests was run against the code before the fix and failed there.

## The layers, and how to run them

| Layer | What it holds | Where | Run it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Unit | the motion math over thousands of seeded inputs: `rubberBand`/`rubberClamp` never pass their reach, are monotonic, continuous at the bounds and undone by their inverses; `arcKeyframes` starts where the thing was, ends exactly at rest, stays inside the box its ends span and bows upward; `flip` starts from the old box, cancels the flight it replaces and divides by its ancestors' scale; `continueTo` turns round from where it is; stagger and exit times; reduced motion maps every movement token to rest in both switches | `motion.property.test.ts`, `../../components/ui/motion.test.ts` (tokens, curves, exits, springs, presses) | `cd app/ui && npx vitest run src/design/motion src/components/ui/motion.test.ts`, or `npm --prefix app test` |
| 2. Component interaction | every primitive and the kit components built on one (Segmented, Switch, Menu, Dialog, Tooltip, Button, StatusLabel, ProgressMeter, ChoiceCards' chips via the same SegmentThumb), driven as a person drives them, in light and dark, full and reduced motion, at 1440 and 390: each comes to rest exactly, once, in its box, nothing still running; nothing in the Motion section is wider than the window; under reduced motion nothing travels, scales, blurs or wipes | `../../../e2e/motion-kit.spec.ts` | `cd app/ui && npx playwright test e2e/motion-kit.spec.ts` |
| 3. Frame by frame | on the lab's controlled clock (`e2e/motionLab.ts`: every CSS and Web Animation paused and stepped 16ms at a time), every frame of every primitive: one pill, inside its track, under every label; at most two layers of a swap or crossfade, never a blink (their opacities composed stay above half), never a double exposure; no restart when re-aimed, toggled ten times, reversed mid-crossfade, closed mid-open or re-rendered mid-arrival; the last frame the resting state exactly. In light at 1440 and dark at 390, under React.StrictMode (the catalog's and the window's), plus What's new's tabs in the real window and the site's hero reel | `../../../e2e/motion-frames.spec.ts`, `../../../e2e/motion.spec.ts`, `tests/test_site_hero_reel.py` | `npx playwright test e2e/motion-frames.spec.ts e2e/motion.spec.ts`; `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_site_hero_reel.py` (needs `bun run build` in `site/`) |
| 4. Visual regression | the start, middle and end frames of the pill, the switch, the crossfade, the swap, the reveal, the arc and the menu, in light and dark, against committed baselines with 1% tolerance. Text glyphs are hidden (`e2e/motion-shots.css`) so the shots compare geometry; native font metrics still affect wrapping, so macOS and Linux keep separate baselines | `../../../e2e/motion-visual.spec.ts`, baselines in `e2e/__screenshots__/motion-visual.spec.ts/` | check: `npx playwright test e2e/motion-visual.spec.ts`; after a deliberate change, look at the diff in `test-results/`, then `npm --prefix app run motion:shots:update` |
| 5. Performance | statically, no stylesheet, keyframe or class transitions a layout property (width, height, top, margin, padding, ...) outside a listed, reasoned exception that may only shrink, and never in the primitives; in the browser, every animation that runs during layer 2's tour animates only compositor (transform, translate, scale, opacity, filter, clip-path) or paint-only properties. `e2e/agents-perf.spec.ts` keeps its frame-time budget | `motion.perf.test.ts`; `e2e/motion-kit.spec.ts`; `e2e/agents-perf.spec.ts` | `npm --prefix app test`; `npx playwright test e2e/agents-perf.spec.ts` (on its own on a busy machine) |
| 6. Accessibility | the OS's reduced motion reaches the catalog and the window before the first paint (`data-motion`, and Zephium's `data-reduce-motion`); focus follows the arrow keys with the pill and never drops to the page mid-flight; the menu and the dialog hold focus while they move and give it back to their trigger; a press mid-flight counts at once; a leaving layer is `aria-hidden` and takes no clicks; a closing dialog's backdrop lets the page be pressed at once | `../../../e2e/motion-a11y.spec.ts` | `npx playwright test e2e/motion-a11y.spec.ts` |

All of the browser layers at once: `npm --prefix app run test:motion` (the
motion unit tests, the build, every `e2e/motion*` spec). The full CI run is
`npm --prefix app run test:e2e`.

## The defects

| # | What | Why | The test that catches it | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Re-aimed mid-flight, the arc's dot (any `SharedLayout` with a `layoutKey`) jumped back to where its first flight began, 250px away, and flew again | `flip()` read the new place with the old flight still running, so the new flight started from the old one's start | frames: "the arc: carries on when sent back mid-flight" (jumped 253px before) | `flip` cancels the flight it replaces before reading the new place (a `WeakMap` of flights), and a cancelled flight's late event no longer clears the new one's `transform-origin` |
| M2 | The tab pill set off a pixel backwards and wobbled | the option it flew into was still shrunk to 0.97 by the press; a translate measured on screen ran inside that scale | frames: "is one pill ... lands exactly" (moves one way only); unit: "divides a distance on screen by the scale its ancestors have" | `flip` divides by its ancestors' scale; in a `motion-segments` track an option's press shrinks its words, not the option, so the pill is never scaled mid-flight |
| M3 | The pill covered the words of the tab it was leaving (they vanished until it had passed) | each option is a stacking context (a kit Button has `will-change: scale`; Segmented and the chips had `isolate`), so the pill inside the new option painted over every option before it | frames: "covers an option's words" at every frame, and What's new's tabs in `motion.spec.ts` | `motion-segments` on the track: the option holding the pill sits under the others (`z-index` 0 under 1), so other options' words are always above it |
| M4 | An icon changed back mid-crossfade flickered: the layers jumped (0.5 to 1, 0.4 to 0) and started over | the layers were CSS keyframes keyed on `data-crossfade`; a keyframe starts from its `from` every time | frames: "reversed mid-change, both layers turn round where they are" (jumped 0.71 before) | Crossfade and Swap layers are Web Animations started from the element's current computed values (`continueTo`, `layerMotion`), taking as long to turn back as they have to go |
| M5 | Counting up fast piled up copies of the old value; a leaving layer could be dropped early | every change added a leaving layer, kept until its own `animationend` (which also bubbled up from any child's animation) or a timer | frames: "counted up fast, two layers at most", "changed six times in a row, never more than two layers" | at most one leaving layer (the one before it goes at once), a stable DOM order so a returning key is the same element turning round, and a layer is dropped on its own animation's `finished` |
| M6 | The arc's dot flew out over the top of its card | the arc bowed off the chord at right angles, and between two corners of a box that is outside the box | unit: "stays inside the box its two ends span"; frames: the dot inside its card at every frame | `arcKeyframes` leans its control point toward the upper corner of the box the two ends span: still an upward bow, never outside that box |
| M7 | The rubber band's badge went 50px out of its track and sat there; grabbed mid spring-back it jumped; a lost pointer capture left it stuck out | the specimen's bounds were 0..0 with a 90px reach and nothing clipped; a new drag started from the target, not from where it was; only `pointerup`/`pointercancel` let go | frames: "past its end it resists, shows only inside its track, springs back exactly, and a grab mid spring-back holds it", "a lost pointer capture lets go"; unit: the inverse properties | `useRubberBand({ within: "parent" })`: bounds from its box, reach a quarter of it, the track clips; a grab reads the on-screen offset and starts from its inverse (`rubberUnclamp`); `lostpointercapture` releases |
| M8 | Old and new were drawn on top of each other: a swap's old value, a crossfade's old icon and the hero reel's old job stayed at nearly full strength while the new one arrived over them | they left on `--ease-exit`, which starts slowly: for the first third of the change nothing had left | frames: "the swap hands over" and "the crossfade hands over" (a double exposure of 0.68 and 0.80 before, now under 0.3 and 0.45); pytest: "a roll never flickers ... and lands exactly" | the one leaving fades on `--ease-out` in an exit's time and moves with the one arriving (Swap's whole time; the reel's `--motion-roll`); the reel's new job fades in at once so the line never blinks empty |
| M9 | On What's new, choosing a tab that shortened the list sent the pill flying in from 97px above its row | the dialog re-centred in the same change, and the pill was measured on the screen, not in its track | `motion.spec.ts`: "What's new's tab pill: one pill, inside its tabs" | `SharedLayout` measures against its `motion-segments` track (or any `data-layout-root`): when the track moves, the pill moves with it and flies only the way it moved inside it |
| M10 | The progress meter animated its fill's `width`, laying the page out again every frame | it was written that way | static: `motion.perf.test.ts`; browser: layer 2's animated-properties check; frames: "the pulse and the meter rest exactly" | the fill and the flight span the track and are clipped to their share with `clip-path` |
| M11 | The catalog's reduced view was not the window's: Zephium's durations kept running | `kit/main.tsx` set `data-motion` only, where `theme-boot.js` sets `data-reduce-motion` too | a11y: "the OS's reduced motion reaches the catalog as the window's" | the catalog sets both |
| M12 | A closing dialog's backdrop (and any leaving surface) caught clicks for its whole exit | the surfaces kept `pointer-events` while `[data-ending-style]` | a11y: "its leaving backdrop takes no clicks" | every motion surface on its way out is `pointer-events: none` |
| M13 | A switch toggled quickly snapped its stretch back to 1 at every press | the stretch was a CSS keyframe restarted by flipping `data-travel` | frames: the switch's "turns" (1.014 then 1 before) | `useKnob` runs the stretch as a Web Animation from the width it has (`stretchKnob`); the crossing stays a transition, which already turns round |
| M14 | A reveal toggled mid-wipe jumped to fully open (or closed) and wiped again | the wipe was a CSS keyframe keyed on `data-reveal` | frames: "the reveal: closed mid-wipe and opened again mid-close" (a 14% jump before) | `revealMotion` (a Web Animation from where the wipe is); unmounts on its own `finished` |
| M15 | Changed again just after a change, a swap blinked nearly empty | a layer turned round early took a share of the time it had run, so an arriving layer barely there was gone in 26ms | frames: "counted up fast" (the composed opacity stays above half) | a fade turned round takes the share of its time that its opacity still has to go |
| M16 | A swap's leaving value showed outside its line, over a button's border | `motion-swap` did not clip | frames: "nothing outside the button" | `motion-swap` clips its block axis (`overflow-y: clip`) |
| M17 | `motionMs()` said it shortened to the reduced fade and did not | the doc and the code had parted | unit: "make every exit 80% of its entrance, and the short fade under reduced motion" | it returns `--motion-reduced` under reduced motion |
| M18 | The sidebar's edge, grabbed again mid spring-back, jumped 16px in to its widest (the edge left the pointer) and kept sliding while held; 380ms after the release the panel's 200ms width transition came back on mid-drag, so the edge trailed the hand | the drag started from the width clamped to its bounds, not from where the edge was; the spring back's inline transition stayed under the new drag; its tidy-up timer was never cleared and removed the drag's `transition-duration: 0ms` with it | `motion.spec.ts`: "the sidebar's edge: grabbed mid spring-back it stays where it is, and then follows the pointer with no tween for the whole drag" (16px, then "0.2s" while held, before) | the session starts from the width on screen, the drag pulls on from its inverse (`rubberUnclamp`, as `useRubberBand` does), a new drag removes the spring back's transition and clears its timer |
| M19 | A `Swap` to a shorter word (a status from "Needs you" to "Done", "Saving…" to "Saved") held its line at the old width for the whole swap, then let go in one frame: everything after it jumped 31px a swap's time after the change | both layers sat in the same grid cell, so the leaving one kept the cell wide until it was dropped | frames: "the swap: to a shorter word, the line takes its new width at once and never snaps when the old one goes" | the leaving layer is lifted out of the line (`data-swap-lifted`, absolute at the width it had, so it does not rewrap) before the first paint; the line reflows once, as the change starts; turned round, it is back in |
| M20 | Clicked again mid-flight, the tab pill stopped dead for about four frames at every click, then set off again: clicking fast across tabs, it stuttered | every flight, a re-aimed one included, ran on `--ease-in-out` from rest, whose first frames barely move (0 to 0.7px a frame after moving 3.5px a frame) | frames: "re-aimed the same way mid-flight, it keeps its speed: no stall at the click"; unit: "re-aimed while moving, sets off at the speed it had, never past its end" | `flip` reads the speed of the flight it replaces (`flightVelocity`, kept with the box when the old element unmounts) and starts the new one at that speed towards its new end (`easeFrom`: the same landing, control points inside 0..1 so it never overshoots); turned back, it starts from rest |
| M21 | At 6x CPU, a theme picked in Settings > Appearance took 240-480ms to paint the click, and anything moving then (the Animation pill, a card's ring) was held: the main thread was blocked ~260ms | every token is on `<html>`, so a theme restyles the whole page (~10-15ms of style unthrottled, 80-190ms at 6x), and it did it twice: inside the click, with t3code's `.no-transitions` put on `<html>`, and again two frames later, taking it off (a second 60-160ms task) | `settings.spec.ts`: "at 6x CPU a theme change paints the choice first and restyles the page once, after it" (the first frame showed the new theme already; `<html>` changed twice, its class on and off) | `withoutTransitions` (design/theme.ts) changes `<html>` once and finishes the transitions running then (`document.getAnimations()`), with no class to take off; Appearance shows the card chosen at once and applies the theme after that frame has painted (`afterPaint`). Measured at 6x: the click paints in 104-152ms (240-480 before), one restyle task of 100-220ms after it instead of 140-290 inside the click plus 60-160 after |
| M22 | On What's new, a tab's rows arrived late and out of order from the top: Improved's first row waited 360ms, Fixed's rows 300ms and more | a row's stagger place (`--i`) was its index in the whole list, and a hidden row shown again replays its `motion-enter` with that delay | `whats-new.spec.ts`: "a tab's rows arrive in order from the top of what it shows; rows already showing stay still" (row 0 of Improved: 360ms before) | `--i` is the row's place in the list as filtered; rows already showing keep their finished arrival (only a hidden row shown again starts it) |
| M23 | A Segmented with long labels at 390px wrapped its words onto two and three lines, spilling out of the 28px option and over the track | the track was `w-fit` with no limit and the labels could wrap | `motion-kit.spec.ts`: "a segmented control with long labels keeps each on one line, in its option, at 390px" (3 lines before), and at 1440px (nothing cut) | the track never grows past its container (`max-w-full`), its options are grid columns of `minmax(0, max-content)` (a short label keeps its whole width, the long ones share the rest), a label is one line cut with an ellipsis, and an option cut short says its whole label on hover (`title`). The catalog's "Segmented, long labels" row shows it |
| M24 | A menu's switch row (`MenuCheckboxItem variant="switch"`) only slid its knob when it kept its own state: no stretch, unlike the Switch | `useKnob` was keyed on `checked`, which an uncontrolled row (`defaultChecked`) never changes | `motion-kit.spec.ts`: "a menu's switch row stretches its knob as it crosses, like the Switch, and rests at 1" (scale 1 at every frame before) | as in `Switch`: uncontrolled, the row's own presses key `useKnob`. The catalog's Menu has a switch row |
| P1 | The visual baselines could not see a pill, a knob, a card or a menu: a shot with no pill, the pill on the wrong tab, no switch knob, the reveal's card 30px off or the arc's dot elsewhere matched its baseline | those are a few levels of grey on grey, under the comparison's colour `threshold` (0.2), and the shots hide text, the only ink there was | a mutation run (each of those injected into the built catalog) failed none of the shots before, and fails them now | `e2e/motion-shots.css` outlines what moves (the shared element, the knob, the reveal, the menu) in the text's colour, inside its box |
| P2 | "a lost pointer capture lets go" failed one full run in several | `settle()` looked for running animations before the change had made one (React's commit and the style recalculation come a frame later), found none, and measured the start of the spring back as its rest | the same test, run in the full suite | `settle()` waits two frames before it looks |

Not defects, looked at and left: Base UI hands focus back to a menu's
trigger once its exit has finished (focus stays in the fading menu for its
160ms, never on the page), and a tooltip's positioner still animates
`top`/`left` between triggers (Base UI's, listed in `motion.perf.test.ts`).

Linux baselines can be authored on an AWS runner with `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch> -f motion_baselines=true`. This manual mode only uploads a review artifact; it never commits files or qualifies a production deployment. Review the start, middle and end images before committing them under the platform directory. Normal CI only compares against committed baselines.
